clue.text: Endless alcohol added to the cold mixed drink

indicators.note: mixed tells us the letters gathered here are stirred into a new order
endless says the word alcohol loses its final letter

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap

explanation.surface: A barman tops up a cold mixed drink with nearly all the booze he has.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endless' cuts ALCOHOL to ALCOHO; with TO, THE and C (cold) those letters are 'mixed' into the answer. 'added' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweet cocoa beverage served warm is a classic example of a drink.

clue.text: Type of degree obtained during working hours? On the contrary

indicators.note: obtained during signals one piece being placed within another
On the contrary flips the stated order, so it is working that goes inside hours, not the reverse

parts.note: taken as written
on means working, as a machine that is switched on

explanation.surface: A student earns a degree by studying in office hours, or so it seems.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface invites putting the degree inside working hours; 'On the contrary' tells you to swap which piece goes inside which.
explanation.definitionFit: A British university bachelor's degree is classed as an honours degree or an ordinary pass.

clue.text: Bright idea, albeit Diderot's last

parts.note: albeit means although, or though

indicators.note: last picks out the final letter of the philosopher's name

explanation.surface: A clever notion, even if it was the French philosopher Diderot's final one.
explanation.definitionFit: A bright idea is a notion or inspiration, something conceived in the mind.

clue.text: Female's male progeny welcoming death of Bellow's hero

indicators.note: welcoming means taking a guest in, so one piece holds another

parts.note: her is the female possessive
end means death, as in meeting one's end
a son is male offspring

explanation.surface: A woman's son greets a death in the family, apparently linked to some hero.
explanation.walkthrough: Eugene HENDERSON is the hero of Saul Bellow's novel Henderson the Rain King.
explanation.definitionFit: Saul Bellow wrote the novel Henderson the Rain King, whose title character is its protagonist.

clue.text: He painted avian bearing right

indicators.note: bearing means carrying, so the bird holds the letter inside it

parts.note: a coot is a water bird, so avian stands for it

explanation.surface: An artist painted a bird flying on a rightward bearing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bearing' looks like a compass direction but means carrying: COOT carries R.
explanation.definitionFit: Jean-Baptiste-Camille Corot was a nineteenth-century French landscape painter.

clue.text: Pan of meat and wine I dropped

parts.note: lamb is a kind of meat

indicators.note: dropped means the named letter is let go from the wine

parts.note: Asti is an Italian sparkling wine

explanation.surface: A frying pan of meat, and a bottle of wine that I let fall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pan' is a verb, to criticise harshly, not a cooking vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: To pan a show is to criticise it severely, the same as to berate it fiercely.

clue.text: Farm work for the pre-senescent?

parts.note: read as ..., the word suggests 'up until old age', fitting those not yet senescent

explanation.surface: Agricultural labour is recommended for people who have not yet grown old.
explanation.definitionFit: Tilling, ploughing and cultivating the soil is the farm work the word names.

clue.text: It sticks out of rolled gold pipe stuck into strut

indicators.note: stuck into says one piece is pushed inside another

parts.note: to prance is to strut showily

indicators.note: rolled means turned over, so the heraldic gold is read backwards

parts.note: or is gold in heraldry
a tube is a pipe

explanation.surface: A gold pipe that has been rolled up and jammed into a strut juts out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rolled' makes RO; heraldic tinctures such as or (gold) are a crossword staple.
explanation.definitionFit: A bulge or swelling projecting from a surface is something that sticks out.

clue.text: City managed to continue

parts.note: ran means managed, as one runs a business
go on means to continue

explanation.surface: A city carried on running as it had been managed.
explanation.definitionFit: Rangoon is the former name of Yangon, the largest city in Myanmar.

clue.text: Rose proves less than coherent speaker

definitions.meaning: a climbing variety of rose plant
someone who talks on and on, wandering off the point

explanation.surface: Getting up proves that someone is not speaking very clearly.
explanation.definitionFit: A climbing rose variety, and also one who rambles, talking at length without focus.

clue.text: Cuter knitter producing something to get one thither and hither

definitions.text: something to get one thither and hither

indicators.note: producing hints that the knitter's letters are worked up into something new

explanation.surface: A cuter knitter makes an item to help someone travel there and back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'thither and hither' means there and back, the trip this travel document covers.
explanation.definitionFit: A travel document covering the journey out and the way back again.

clue.text: Get a grip on girl's head in support of ritual murder

indicators.note: in places the gripping and the head of the girl inside the support

parts.note: a tee is a golf ball's support
to hug is to get a grip on someone

indicators.note: head picks out the first letter of the girl

explanation.surface: A thug grabs a girl by the head as part of some violent ritual.
explanation.walkthrough: THUGGEE was the practice of robbery and ritual strangling by the Thugs of India.
explanation.definitionFit: The Thugs of India carried out robbery and strangulation as a religious rite.

clue.text: Bitter (twisted) about exile's old car

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the twisted word goes round the exile
twisted means turned round, so the bitter word is read backwards

parts.note: tart means sour or bitter
to ban is to exile someone

explanation.surface: A bitter, warped exile with a battered old vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twisted' reverses TART to TRAT, which goes 'about' BAN.
explanation.definitionFit: The Trabant was the small two-stroke car made in former East Germany.

clue.text: Invest last bit of revenue in cream

indicators.note: in places the final letter of revenue inside the cream

parts.note: the cream is the best of something

indicators.note: last bit of picks the final letter of revenue

explanation.surface: Advice to put the final portion of earnings into dairy products.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Invest' is not finance: it is the old sense of besieging or surrounding.
explanation.definitionFit: To invest a town is to surround and besiege it, so the two verbs coincide.

clue.text: Tourist and prophet pursuing vision

indicators.note: pursuing means following behind, so the prophet comes after vision

parts.note: sight is vision
a seer is a prophet

explanation.surface: A tourist and a prophet chase a vision together.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who visits places to view the famous attractions is a tourist.

clue.text: Novice hag wasting time where it's monitored?

parts.note: green means inexperienced, a novice

indicators.note: wasting means losing, so time is taken out of the hag

parts.note: a witch is a hag

explanation.surface: A newly trained old crone loses track of time wherever she is watched.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' is time: GREENWICH, in London, gives Greenwich Mean Time and the Royal Observatory.
explanation.definitionFit: Greenwich in London is home of the Royal Observatory and the zero meridian of world time.

clue.text: Home team in not entirely recent reshuffle

indicators.note: in places the team inside the reshuffled letters
reshuffle means the letters are rearranged
not entirely says the word recent loses its last letter

parts.note: a side is a team

explanation.surface: A team is housed in a home after a recent squad reshuffle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not entirely' trims to RECEN, and 'reshuffle' rearranges that to RENCE before the team goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: A residence is a dwelling, the place where one lives.

clue.text: A youngster, by degrees, raised drink

indicators.note: raised in a down answer means the pieces read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: a cub is a young animal or youngster
MAs are Master of Arts degrees

explanation.surface: Someone young who rose degree by degree ended up with a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' is a link; 'raised' reads A CUB MAS upwards, from the bottom of the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: Sambuca is an Italian aniseed-flavoured liqueur, served as a drink.

clue.text: Country retreat given notice

parts.note: a den is a private retreat
mark means notice, as in mark my words

explanation.surface: A country retreat is given its notice to quit.
explanation.definitionFit: Denmark is a Scandinavian nation in northern Europe.

clue.text: Bird is good in bed

parts.note: pi is short for pious, so good
pit is slang for bed

explanation.surface: A bird is happy tucked up in bed.
explanation.definitionFit: The pipit is a small brown songbird, rather like a lark.

clue.text: Scope to wire up 5, ineptly

indicators.note: ineptly means clumsily done, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: Someone told to connect five things is clumsy about it.
explanation.walkthrough: '5' is the Roman numeral V, not a reference to clue 5.
explanation.definitionFit: Purview is the range or extent of something's authority, its scope.

clue.text: Oracular snake dropping round for 1A?

indicators.note: dropping the round letter in favour of something else signals a swap

parts.note: a python is a snake
1A is read as one plus A, so I and A

explanation.surface: A clue swapping a snake for the drink in 1 Across.
explanation.walkthrough: '1A' looks like a cross-reference to HOT CHOCOLATE, but is read as I (one) and A; they replace the O (round).
explanation.definitionFit: Pythian refers to the Pythia, the oracle priestess of Apollo at Delphi.

clue.text: About time to adopt compiler's candidate

indicators.note: to adopt means taking in, so the time word holds the compiler's
About means turned around, so the time word reads backwards

parts.note: an eon is a long period of time
mine is the compiler's, the setter's own

explanation.surface: Roughly when it is time for the setter to adopt their chosen candidate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' reverses EON to NOE, which takes in MINE.
explanation.definitionFit: A nominee is a person put forward for a post, a candidate.

clue.text: Hard up?

parts.note: 'Hard up' looks like short of money but means firm and standing upright

explanation.surface: A question about whether someone is short of money.
explanation.definitionFit: Standing upright and stiff, rigid and vertical.

clue.text: One cretin floundering near the coast

indicators.note: floundering means struggling confusedly, so the letters are in a mess

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A fool is floundering in the shallows near the shore.
explanation.definitionFit: Neritic describes shallow coastal waters over the continental shelf.

clue.text: Attempt to match bird no longer with us

parts.note: an emu is a large flightless bird
late means deceased, no longer with us

explanation.surface: An effort to equal a bird that has died.
explanation.definitionFit: To try to match or rival someone is to copy their achievements.

clue.text: Shed is en voyage in colour

parts.note: Shed is the setter, so refers to himself as I

indicators.note: en is French for in, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: a ride is a journey or trip
taken as written

explanation.surface: The setter goes travelling, described in French.
explanation.walkthrough: Guardian setters often name themselves, so 'Shed' means 'I'; 'en' is French borrowed as a container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To iridise is to give rainbow-like shimmering hues to something.

clue.text: Interrogate and masticate, independently entering Devil's Province

indicators.note: independently says the second verb goes into the Devil by itself, separately
entering means going inside, so a verb goes into the Devil

parts.note: Satan is the Devil
to ask is to interrogate
to chew is to masticate

explanation.surface: Questioning and chewing, each going into the Devil's Province.
explanation.walkthrough: ASK and CHEW go into SATAN at separate points: S-ASK-AT-CHEW-AN.
explanation.definitionFit: Saskatchewan is a prairie province of western Canada.
